source.title: A Neural Scaling Law from Lottery Ticket Ensembling

record.tranche_reason: The study reports toy-task scaling sweeps in which curves change shape across activations and tasks, including departures from a single power law.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own MSE-versus-width results on toy function-fitting tasks, which bear on V5 and V7. Its discussion of the Hoffmann et al. language-model exponent is cited prior work, not a result from this study. Lottery-ticket histograms and mechanism analyses are not separately rowed because they do not directly measure a version's scaling behavior.
record.test_reason: The study's own results are MSE-versus-width curves for one-hidden-layer MLPs fitting synthetic 1D functions and products, over widths 10–50 (under one order of magnitude). These are not language-model pretraining loss (V1–V4, V6, V7). Synthetic function regression is also not one of the modalities or training regimes V5 names (image, video, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer). The rows therefore measure a related construct: approximation scaling of tiny networks. The only language-model link is a cited Hoffmann et al. exponent (0.34) compared against the authors' speculative 1/3 prediction, which is not the study's own result.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. To add: the authors report that y=x² gives an empirical N^-1 law, contradicting the approximation-theory prediction of N^-4. They tentatively note that their implied ℓ∝N^-1/3 for language models resembles Hoffmann et al.'s 0.34 exponent, possibly by coincidence. They flag the theory, not the empirical results, as questionable.
record.recipe_differences: Toy supervised regression with two-layer networks and MSE; varies width and studies lottery-ticket ensembling rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported loss-curve shape varies with activation and target task; ReLU/LeakyReLU transitions from an initial N^-4 region to N^-1, while other target functions may plateau or increase.

fits_no_version.finding: One-hidden-layer MLPs fitting y=x² show median MSE ∝ N^-1 (SiLU), and N^-4 then N^-1 (LeakyReLU), over widths 10–50. Other synthetic targets and multiplication tasks follow N^-1 only partly, or plateau. The authors attribute N^-1 to lottery-ticket ensembling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width-scaling exponents of small networks on synthetic regression depend on activation and target, and can depart from approximation-theory predictions.

record.problems: Evidence is primarily toy function-fitting with one hidden layer and modest width ranges. Curves are shown in figures without numerical tables or reported error bars; the paper uses medians over 1000 seeds. The authors themselves flag possible optimization issues, bias effects, and limited generality.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for the lottery-ticket loss histograms, neuron analyses, ensembling comparison, or distilled networks: those results address the proposed mechanism rather than directly reporting the scaling measures covered by the versions.

untested.parts: No language models or pretraining loss.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No image, video, repeated-data, fine-tuning or transfer settings; only synthetic function regression.
No language-model laws, parameter counting, schedules or fitting methods compared.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests' and T5 overstate relevance: toy MLP width sweeps spanning a factor of 5 do not measure what any version names. The Hoffmann exponent comparison is a cited result plus speculation. Several appendix row assignments (sin, cos, exp, relu) are inferred rather than stated in the text.

versions.untested_parts: No language models or held-out pretraining cross-entropy are tested.
No small-run fits are used to predict the losses of larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between parameter count and training tokens is tested.
The study does not compare depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count; width is varied in a one-hidden-layer network.
Tests toy supervised function fitting with MSE, not other modalities such as image or video, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No downstream tasks or relationship between pretraining loss and downstream performance are tested.
Shows dependence on task and activation and curves that bend or plateau, but does not vary parameter-count conventions, fitting methods, or compute-optimal allocation.
